description: String-heavy corpus that is deliberately hostile to zero-copy UTF-8 parsing: every entry mixes escape sequences with literal multi-byte UTF-8.

entries.title: He said "the parser must not copy", and then said "but it does"
entries.body: The reviewer wrote: "a value containing \"nested quotes\" defeats the fast path". That is the point of this entry.
entries.note: Backslashes and quotes only, no multi-byte characters.

entries.title:
Tabs	and	newlines
in a single value
entries.body:
line one
line two
line three
	indented continuation
	another indented line
end of record
entries.note: Only \n and \t appear; \r is intentionally absent so the record stays platform-neutral.

entries.title: Escaped code points: éèêë üöä ñ
entries.body: Café naïve façade — written entirely with \uXXXX escapes so the decoder must expand them: “quoted”, ‘single’, ellipsis… and a non-breaking space.
entries.note: Every accented character here is a \uXXXX escape, not a literal byte sequence.

entries.title: Literal two-byte UTF-8: éèêë üöä ñ ç å ø
entries.body: Der Prüfstand läuft über Nacht. La città è già pronta. El niño comió mañana. Æther, Ångström, Œuvre — all written as literal UTF-8 bytes rather than escapes.
entries.note: Two-byte sequences only; contrast with the previous entry, which encodes the same characters as escapes.

entries.title: 三字节 UTF-8 序列：中文、日本語、한국어
entries.body: これはベンチマーク用のドキュメントです。解析器は三バイトの UTF-8 シーケンスを処理する必要があります。这段文字用于测试解析器对多字节字符的处理速度。이 문서는 파서 성능 측정을 위한 것입니다。
entries.note: Three-byte sequences dominate this record; the byte length is far larger than the character count.

entries.title: Four-byte sequences: 🚀 🔥 🧪 📊 🐛
entries.body: Deploy went out 🚀, the dashboard lit up 📊, then the on-call pager fired 🔥 and we found the bug 🐛 in the parser fast path 🧪. Surrogate pairs in UTF-16, four bytes in UTF-8.
entries.note: Emoji are outside the basic multilingual plane, so a UTF-16 decoder must produce surrogate pairs.

entries.title: Surrogate-pair escapes: 🚀 🔥 📊
entries.body: The same astral characters as the previous entry, but written as \uXXXX surrogate pairs: 🚀 launch, 🧪 test, 🐛 bug. A parser must recombine the pairs.
entries.note: Exercises the surrogate-pair branch of the escape decoder.

entries.title: Mixed: "quoted" \ backslash 	 tab, café 中文 🚀 and é 中 🚀
entries.body:
Every hostile construct in one value: an escaped quote \", a literal backslash \\, a tab	character, a newline\n rendered literally as two characters, a real newline
here, escaped Latin é, literal Latin é, escaped CJK 中, literal CJK 中, escaped emoji 🚀, literal emoji 🚀.
entries.note: This is the record that should defeat every zero-copy shortcut.

entries.title: Control record: no escapes, no multi-byte characters
entries.body: This value is long, plain, and entirely ASCII, so the zero-copy path applies to it. Having it in the same document means the corpus is not uniformly hostile, and a measurement can separate the cost of the escape slow path from the cost of simply having long string values to hand back. The sentence continues for a while so that its length is comparable to the hostile records above and the comparison is not confounded by size.
entries.note: Baseline for the records around it.

entries.title: Many short strings
entries.body: Short values stress per-value overhead rather than per-byte throughput.

entries.title: Embedded JSON and URLs
entries.body: {"nested":"a JSON document encoded inside a string value","count":42,"unicode":"café 中文 🚀"}
entries.note: Escaped braces and quotes appear inside a value, which forces the escape path without any multi-byte bytes.
